text:
zoe: Noticed a pile of tiny-gang pods stuck Pending in us-west1 for the last ~45m. Symptoms look like scheduler bias toward the anchored GPU pool + strict nodeSelector for `gpu.shape=a100-small`.

rahul: Do the nodes actually have that label across AZs? We patched a node flavor label change last week.

zoe: I dumped nodes: `kubectl get nodes -L gpu.shape -o wide | grep us-west1` and only us-west1-a shows `a100-small`. us-west1-b/c are `a100-medium` and `a100-large`. Scheduler logs show PreferentialAffinity hooking on nodepool affinity.

tess: Output paste:```
NAME                        STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION   gpu.shape
us-west1-a-node-01          Ready    <none>   22d   v1.27     a100-small
us-west1-b-node-11          Ready    <none>   12d   v1.27     a100-medium
us-west1-c-node-21          Ready    <none>   5d    v1.27     a100-large
```

rahul: Ah, that explains it. The pod's PodSpec has `nodeSelector: gpu.shape: a100-small` because the model runtime was tuned to a small instance. But most tenants are now using medium/large shapes; our admission controller sets that selector for legacy workloads.

zoe: kube-scheduler events for one pending pod: `0/24 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 8 node(s) didn't match nodeSelector, 6 node(s) had taints the pod didn't tolerate.`

ops-jen: There's also a scheduling extender in the fleet that applies a hard score bump (+1000) if a node is in the anchored pool to keep latency-sensitive inference on that pool. The extender doesn't consider nodeSelector mismatches properly, causing heavy skew.

rahul: Two immediate options: 1) relax nodeSelector via a mutation admission for the tiny-gang class to accept any `a100-*` shape; 2) temporarily disable the anchored-pool hard bump. Which is lower risk?

tess: Option 1 is safer: mutate only pods with label `workload-class=tiny-gang` to replace nodeSelector with a `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` nodeAffinity that prefers a100-small but allows other shapes. We'll limit to ml namespace.

zoe: Can you show the patch you propose?

tess: Patch snippet:```
kubectl patch poddefaults tiny-gang-default -n ml -p '{"spec":{"nodeSelector":null,"affinity":{"nodeAffinity":{"preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution":[{"weight":50,"preference":{"matchExpressions":[{"key":"gpu.shape","operator":"In","values":["a100-small","a100-medium","a100-large"]}]}}]}}}}'
```

infra-bot: patch job queued by tess: poddefaults/tiny-gang-default; CI run id infra-patch-1761234568; monitor at https://ci.redwood/patches/infra-patch-1761234568

rahul: Also FYI the autoscaler cooldown prevented warm-pool spinup earlier today: warm-pool controller logs show `replicas unchanged: desired=0 current=3 cooldown=true` because of ENG-INFRA-999 throttling rule. We'll need to relax cooldown for ml namespace during heavy spike windows.

zoe: After applying the mutation to ml-canary, 8/10 pending pods scheduled across b/c within 2m. No immediate latency regressions reported from canary traces.

tess: I'll roll the change to ml-prod with a 10m canary. Also opening ENG-SCHED-420 to track removing the anchoring hard-bump and replacing with soft bias that respects nodeSelector and nodeAffinity scoring.

ops-jen: Long-term, we should deprecate auto-applied nodeSelector in admission and move to flavor hints that admission converts to preferred affinities. That avoids strict mismatches when the fleet diversifies.

rahul: Cost note: if we allow pods to land on larger shapes, GPU-hours per inference may increase ~4% due to lower packing efficiency. But it beats 30% latency spikes while waiting for anchored slots. We'll track impact under COST-301.

infra-bot: Incident ticket created INF-1761234568: stranded-tiny-gang-due-to-nodeSelector; assignees: tess, rahul; sla: 4h.

zoe: Closing loop after prod rollout. Will post a short runbook update: - How to detect nodeSelector-induced skew - Temporary mutate command - Watching instructions for oncall (alerts: ProdPendingRate>50/min AND AZ skew > 50%).

tess: Thanks everyone. Will follow up with ENG-SCHED-420 draft tomorrow. :sparkles:
